recent_posts.title: Predicted backlash against human data labeling for AI training
recent_posts.summary: AI companies are paying professionals across various fields to label data and train models through reinforcement learning, essentially transferring human expertise to AI systems. This creates a prisoner's dilemma where workers contribute to systems that may eventually replace them. A potential backlash is predicted, either through regulatory action or public protest, as society grapples with the moral implications of paying individuals to train AI systems that could eliminate jobs for entire professions.

recent_posts.title: The 2026 Recruiting Reckoning & AI Predictions
recent_posts.summary: Two recruiting industry experts discuss predictions for how AI will transform talent acquisition in 2026. Key forecasts include: VC talent partners moving in-house to AI companies, AI becoming the default first screen for job applicants, 90% of sourcing being automated while outreach automation fails, the emergence of 'agent manager' roles, shrinking tech headcount causing social unrest among displaced workers, and foundation AI labs moving deeper into business applications. They emphasize that 2026 will shift from AI hype to demonstrable agent performance and substance.

recent_posts.title: Executive coaching requires real operational experience
recent_posts.summary: Executive coaching requires real operational experience to be effective. Many coaches lack actual arena experience, having only completed weekend certification programs without ever operating at executive levels. When selecting a coach, prioritize those who have direct experience with your specific challenges—startup CEOs need coaches who have built startups, not just worked with Fortune 100 companies. The credibility gap between certified coaches and experienced operators undermines the coaching industry's value.

recent_posts.title: Experience vs. credentials: the coach balance #substack #shorts
recent_posts.summary: Coaching effectiveness relies more on practical experience than formal credentials. Clients prioritize real-world experience and the ability to navigate challenges based on past situations. The most effective coaching approach balances asking questions and challenging assumptions with providing concrete advice drawn from experience, rather than relying solely on either method.

recent_posts.title: Building an executive coaching business with transparent revenue numbers
recent_posts.summary: Executive coach Nathan Tanner shares transparent revenue figures from his coaching business, revealing $142K in his first year and $335K in his second year after leaving a $240K tech salary. He emphasizes that successful coaching requires real operator experience over weekend certifications, with most clients coming through referrals rather than marketplaces. Tanner charges varied rates targeting underserved startup CEOs, maintains 11-16 clients simultaneously, and structures six-month engagements that typically last just over one year before clients graduate.

recent_posts.title: Why Comp Negotiations Fall Apart (No Bedrock) #shorts
recent_posts.summary: Compensation negotiations often fail without an agreed-upon process. While benchmarking tools like Carta provide ownership data, every company is unique and requires recognizing individual perspectives. Establishing a compensation philosophy and fair process before discussing specific numbers creates a foundation for acceptance of outcomes and prevents negotiations from devolving into arbitrary requests.

recent_posts.title: Blitzscaling's Chris Yeh on Infinite Learning, Staying Cool, and Building Strategic Networks
recent_posts.summary: Chris Yeh shares insights on maintaining relevance through continuous learning and unlearning, building strategic networks with younger generations, and assessing startup opportunities. He discusses blitzscaling principles, emphasizing adaptability over headcount growth, and explains how employees should evaluate companies using an investor mindset. Key advice includes negotiating founder equity by establishing fair processes before discussing numbers, assessing founders through extended shared experiences, and offering compensation packages with multiple salary-to-equity ratios to create mutual value.

recent_posts.title: Zapier's four level AI fluency framework for employees
recent_posts.summary: Zapier uses a four-level AI fluency rubric to evaluate employees: unacceptable (lacking skills and motivation), capable (basic AI application skills), adaptive (using AI to improve conventional workflows), and transformational (reimagining work processes from scratch using AI). The transformational level represents the highest tier, where individuals completely rethink how work gets done rather than just optimizing existing methods.

recent_posts.title: Zapier + LLM: Practical Coaching #substack #shorts
recent_posts.summary: A demonstration of using Zapier with LLMs to automate coaching feedback from one-on-one meeting transcripts. The system uses custom code steps (written by non-developers with LLM assistance) to structure transcripts, calculate talk-to-listen ratios, and provide thematic feedback over time by storing data across multiple sessions.

recent_posts.title: Using AI to provide automated feedback for managers at scale
recent_posts.summary: AI-powered tools can scale HR business partner functions by recording manager interactions and providing automated feedback. The system analyzes meetings to tell managers what they did well and where they can improve, while giving HR visibility into management practices they normally can't observe. This addresses the widespread challenge of poor management by making feedback continuous and data-driven.

top_posts.summary: Learn about the common mistakes that companies make with remote work, how remote handles compensation for employees in different countries, and the challenges of employee mobility in a remote work setting.

top_posts.title: Transforming Recruiting with Custom GPT and AI Insights #substack #shorts
top_posts.summary: A recruiting team at HPIQ1 developed a custom GPT system that analyzes candidate interviews by incorporating company context, organizational charts, and employee bios. The system processes interview transcripts to provide hiring recommendations, identifying green flags, red flags, and cultural fit assessments. Early results suggest the AI analysis may outperform human evaluation, though legal and bias concerns around AI-driven hiring decisions remain significant considerations for organizations.

top_posts.title: Why Greylock's Glen Evans Says Your All-Nighter Culture Is Actually Anti-Growth
top_posts.summary: In Silicon Valley, early-stage founders are adopting intense work cultures, often promoting long hours as a sign of commitment. Glen Evans from Greylock criticizes this approach, suggesting it may deter top talent and lead to burnout. He advocates for creating a culture based on shared purpose, clear goals, and inspiring leadership, arguing that success is not merely built on hustle but on belief and intentionality. The discussion also touches on the age-related differences in willingness to engage in such work environments, stressing life is about trade-offs.

top_posts.title: Be an Infinite Learner with Chris Yeh
top_posts.summary: Chris Yeh shares insights on staying energetic and passionate throughout a diverse career. He emphasizes the importance of practicing public speaking, unlearning outdated knowledge, and building a team of infinite learners. Yeh discusses the value of prioritizing tasks over trying to do everything and developing adaptability and resilience in tech. He also highlights the significance of maintaining connections with younger people and staying updated with popular culture to stay relevant.

top_posts.title: How to actually use AI agents, with Samy Aumar of Qonto
top_posts.summary: Samy Aumar from Qonto demonstrates practical AI agent implementation in recruiting workflows using Dust platform. He shows two main use cases: automated job description creation from intake meeting transcripts and market intelligence research for competitor analysis. The setup requires no coding skills and can be built in an afternoon. Qonto implemented an AI mandate with team champions rather than top-down enforcement, achieving 80-100% weekly usage across the company. Key benefits include reducing job posting creation from 2-3 days to 24 hours and eliminating blank page syndrome by providing 85-90% complete outputs that require minimal editing.
